title: Wave-pinning crawler with a self-made adsorbed layer: a species made inside the body collects at the moving interface (signed-distance rim/core 2.3-3.7, rim/out 14-20) while the cell crawls at 0.42 and through a 40% front cut
summary: c22's Camley crawler (rho*=0.2, eta=2, per-body pools) plus a layer species s made inside the body (kp*phi, 97% of production inside phi>1/2), decaying everywhere (kd=0.5), diffusing (Ds=0.1) and adsorbing onto the interface by the diffuse-interface Langmuir flux Ds*beta*s(1-s)*grad(4phi(1-phi)) (beta=4); the operator reproduces the Fermi/Langmuir isotherm on a frozen disk to 83-94% of the predicted odds ratio (isotherm.py, central face flux; first-order upwind gave only 28-64%). On seeds 0-2 (labkit, t=20) the crawler keeps its speed and the s layer scores rim/core 1.9-1.94 and rim/outside 14-14.7 in labkit's radial test, 6/6 individuals (sheet.png, radial.png); the rear rim carries about twice the front's s. After a 40% front cut (seed 0, branched twin) the layer closes over the cut edge within 1 time unit and stays on through c22's flood-renucleate repair path; the cut cell crawls again at 0.35 vs the twin's 0.42.
